content:
IELTS Listening can be the most difficult section in the listening test. This is because by listening this listening part once, students need to finish two parts of questions. In most of the cases, you will need to fill in a form, after that do another five multiple choice questions. Moreover, it is also likely to include other things like sentence completion questions. Casper Academy of Excellence is the leading IELTS coaching centre in Kochi with expert team of trainers who help in getting through this.

This section is made more difficult by the fact that the recording is usually an academic talk about a specific subject, such as biology or history. Let’s look at the best IELTS section 4 listening tips to help you succeed on test day!

Allocate Your Time Wisely

It is critical to allocate your time wisely in the listening section. Try to read all of the questions at the start of the listening section. If you can finish reading section four questions before section one begins, read them again after answering section three, paying special attention to the long choices in multiple choice questions. Practicing the questions ahead of time allows you to focus on the recording! Casper Academy of Excellence is popular as the leading institute to provide IELTS coaching in Kochi.

Circle Key Words

Circle the key words as you read the questions. The key words in the question refer to the most important information. Some key words are obvious, such as an academic term or a name, while others are more subtle. You must pay close attention to the recording for key words.

Predict the Answer

You can sometimes predict the answer based on the information provided, especially in table/form/sentence completion questions. As an example, you can consider British Council question. Practice

Practice makes things more perfect. You can prepare for this section by taking practise tests and listening to academic talks from various websites.
